name: Low-pass out, high-pass in
lesson:
## Two filters, one crossing

B starts with its CFX held right in high-pass and its fader up over 8 bars: only its top end is in the mix. Over bars 9 to 17, B's filter opens back to centre while A's filter closes into low-pass; the two knobs move as mirror images. Kill A's fader on bar 17 and reset its filter.

The crossing keeps the frequency budget honest: as A loses its top end, B gains it; as B gains its bass, A loses it. This is the filter version of a bass swap and needs the same phrase alignment: both filters must reach their end value on bar 17 or the drop has two kicks.
